page: Amazon Web Services m8in.12xlarge is an eighth-generation general-purpose EC2 instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It features a 64-bit x86 Intel processor running at a 3.9 GHz clock speed. The instance allocates 48 dedicated virtual CPUs derived from 24 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading active at two threads per core. System memory totals 192.0 GB of RAM, sustaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU.

Network performance is a defining aspect of the m8in.12xlarge configuration, which provides a 75 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The instance does not feature local instance storage or onboard GPUs, relying exclusively on remote Elastic Block Store volumes for non-volatile persistent storage. This separation requires storage traffic to traverse the Nitro-managed I/O plane alongside general network communication.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the m8in.12xlarge delivers high network throughput alongside substantial general-purpose compute density. Workloads that saturate standard networking bandwidth caps before consuming their compute envelope can operate on this tier without needing to scale to higher-tier CPU counts solely for network headroom. However, the lack of local NVMe storage incurs qualitative cost and architectural tradeoffs when low-latency ephemeral disk caching is required.

The m8in.12xlarge is suited for distributed data processing, intermediate web serving clusters, enterprise resource planning backends, and containerized microservices fleets requiring consistent high-bandwidth inter-node communication.
